strengths: Equipment is represented as a relation on the existing canonical M4 Item Graph item, so item_id, ownership, inventory, snapshot, checksum and durability remain one truth.
Existing Item Graph delta and durable restore paths carried equipment state to two independent replicas and reconnect without any P5-specific replication transport.

ResourceMining capability validation is inserted after existing replay/payload/range ordering and failure is recorded in the existing ResourceMining ledger, preserving exact-once behavior across later equip/unequip changes.
The live dedicated-server product path is switched by one stable composition adapter; M3 transport, persistence, network authority and M7 are untouched.
Legacy live fixtures were adapted by explicit canonical item.equip operations; server auto-equip was deliberately rejected.
risks_and_lessons: Playable-sandbox tool bootstrap changes canonical Item Graph shape. It is sandbox-only, creates one ordinary canonical singleton tool per player, includes stable slot_index, and never auto-equips. Omitting slot_index was caught locally because durable restore changed checksum/revision.

Changing the stable product composition surfaced historical live fixtures that assumed mining required no equipment. Updating those fixtures through the real command path was necessary to prove the new product rule rather than bypass it.

The repository full world/core suite contains inherited stale expectations and SceneTree-invalid tests already present at the exact accepted P4 base; therefore focused GREEN cannot be promoted to FULL_WORLD_CORE_REGRESSION_PASS by interpretation.

open_blockers.requires: separate baseline repair and exact-head rerun; frozen P5 runtime must not be mutated unless the repair proves a P5 defect
